moved.sentence: Per [adc.principle.small-reversible-decisions](cookbook:4554e680-aca3-4bb2-bc99-1ac381c428b2):

judged.note: The rationale keeps the citation of adc.principle.small-reversible-decisions, with its link, as the basis for adopting the stricter flags incrementally on existing code.

moved.sentence: Turn on `strict` first; land that as its own change.

judged.note: Turning on strict first on existing code and landing it as its own change is kept at SHOULD.

moved.sentence: Enable one stricter flag at a time (`noUncheckedIndexedAccess`, then `exactOptionalPropertyTypes`, etc.), fixing the fallout before moving on.

judged.note: Enabling one stricter flag at a time, with the example sequence, and fixing the fallout before moving on are kept at SHOULD.

moved.sentence: Agents **SHOULD NOT** enable every flag in a single sweep on an established codebase — small, reviewable diffs keep each step reversible.
New TypeScript projects **MUST** set `"strict": true` in `tsconfig.json` `compilerOptions`.
Code **MUST NOT** silence the checker with project-wide `// @ts-nocheck`, blanket `any`, or `skipLibCheck` used to hide first-party errors.
Use a narrowly-scoped `// @ts-expect-error` (with a reason) for the rare unavoidable case so the suppression fails loudly if the underlying type later changes.

judged.note: The narrowly-scoped // @ts-expect-error with a reason for the rare unavoidable case, and its fail-loudly reason, are kept at SHOULD.

moved.sentence: `"strictNullChecks": false`) **SHOULD** be treated as a temporary migration state, recorded in code with a tracking reference — not a permanent posture.
Treat the following as roadmap/proposed behavior.

judged.note: Treating the forecast items as roadmap/proposed behavior is kept at SHOULD, with both forecast items listed as sub-points.

moved.sentence: Do **not** write configs or guidance that assume it as current.

judged.note: Not writing configs or guidance that assume the forecast behavior as current is kept at SHOULD NOT.

moved.sentence: The **native Go compiler ("tsgo", "Project Corsa")** and the **TypeScript 7.0** line are a proposed reimplementation targeting large build speedups.

As of this writing, confirm actual release state against the official [TypeScript blog](https://devblogs.microsoft.com/typescript/) and [microsoft/typescript-go](https://github.com/microsoft/typescript-go) before depending on it.

judged.note: Confirming the native Go compiler and TypeScript 7.0 release state against the TypeScript blog and microsoft/typescript-go before depending on it is kept at SHOULD with both links.

moved.sentence: "**strict by default**" and the **removal of legacy module/target modes** (e.g. dropping `node10` resolution, raising the minimum target) are PLANNED breaking changes discussed for the 6.0/7.0 line.
Until you have verified them in shipped release notes, **MUST** keep setting `"strict": true` explicitly rather than relying on an implicit default.

judged.note: The MUST to keep setting "strict": true explicitly until strict-by-default and the legacy-mode removal are verified in shipped release notes is kept, with its condition.

moved.sentence: `exactOptionalPropertyTypes` (TS 4.4) — distinguishes a missing property from one explicitly set to `undefined`.

judged.note: What exactOptionalPropertyTypes (TS 4.4) does, distinguishing a missing property from one set to undefined, is kept as a sub-point.

moved.sentence: Enable when modeling APIs where "absent" and "present but undefined" differ.

judged.note: Enabling exactOptionalPropertyTypes when modeling APIs where absent and present-but-undefined differ is kept at SHOULD with its condition.

moved.sentence: It adds real friction with loosely-typed third-party shapes, so it is **opt-in**, not a baseline.

judged.note: The third-party friction reason and its opt-in, not baseline, status are kept in the rule.

moved.sentence: `erasableSyntaxOnly` (TS 5.8) — errors on TypeScript constructs that emit runtime code (`enum`, `namespace` with runtime members, parameter properties).

judged.note: What erasableSyntaxOnly (TS 5.8) does, with all three runtime-emitting constructs, is kept as a sub-point.

moved.sentence: Enable it when files are run via native type-stripping (Node.js `--experimental-strip-types`/stable type stripping, Bun, Deno, or in-browser transforms) so the source contains no non-erasable syntax.

judged.note: Enabling erasableSyntaxOnly when files run via native type-stripping, with every runtime listed and the no-non-erasable-syntax purpose, is kept at SHOULD.

moved.sentence: Pair it with `verbatimModuleSyntax`.

judged.note: Pairing erasableSyntaxOnly with verbatimModuleSyntax is kept at SHOULD.

moved.sentence: Enable these on greenfield projects; they close gaps `strict` alone leaves open.

judged.note: Enabling the near-default flags on greenfield projects, with the reason that they close gaps strict alone leaves open, is kept in the rule.

moved.sentence: New projects **SHOULD** enable `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` and `verbatimModuleSyntax`.

judged.note: The SHOULD for new projects to enable noUncheckedIndexedAccess and verbatimModuleSyntax is kept verbatim.

moved.sentence: With `verbatimModuleSyntax`, type-only imports **MUST** use `import type` / `export type` (or inline `type` modifiers), since the compiler no longer elides them automatically.
